title: The buttons under a capture say what they do again
goal: Hovering the copy, edit, reveal and delete buttons under a capture in the history overlay shows nothing, so the only way to know what a glyph does is to press it. These had labels on hover before. Bring them back, and make sure the rest of the overlay has them too.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-05 with a screenshot of the history overlay: these buttons do not have tooltips, I thought we had them at one point. The machinery is all present, which is why this is a bug and not a feature: HistoryOverlay.iconButton (line 323) attaches historyTooltip for Copy, Show in Finder and Delete; HistoryTooltipModifier (line 334) reads the button frame through a preference in the overlay coordinate space and calls AppCoordinator.showCaptureTooltip on hover; that method (AppCoordinator.swift line 430) converts the frame to screen coordinates and shows a floating NSPanel through TooltipController. Suspects to check rather than guess: the preference may never deliver a frame so rect stays zero and the panel is positioned off screen; historyOverlay.panelFrame may be nil at hover time so the guard returns silently; the flip from the overlay top down coordinates to screen bottom up at line 433 may be wrong now the overlay layout has changed; or the panel may be ordered behind the overlay window. Note the tool bar took a different route when tooltips landed there, so check whether one shared way to show a tooltip is now warranted rather than two. The edit button in the screenshot is not one of the three that call iconButton, so also confirm every button in that row goes through the same helper.
acceptance: Reproduce the failure first and record in the log what actually happens: whether the hover is never seen, the position is computed wrong so the label appears off screen, or the label is drawn behind the overlay
Hovering any button under a capture shows its label within the usual delay: copy, edit, reveal and delete
The label appears just below the button it belongs to, fully on screen, including for the leftmost and rightmost buttons and for a capture at the edge of the row
The filter and clear all controls at the top of the overlay keep their labels
A short walk or test guards it, so the labels cannot disappear again without something failing
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a picture of a label showing, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: REPRODUCED, in the probe with a scripted walk. The hover IS seen: the button's onHover fires with hovering=true. What is wrong is the frame it hands over. HistoryTooltipModifier reads the icon's rectangle through a SwiftUI preference set inside .background(GeometryReader ...); the GeometryReader itself computes the right rectangle (28x28 at the button's place, confirmed by logging proxy.frame directly), but the preference never reaches the .onPreferenceChange beside it, so the stored frame stays (0,0,0,0) forever. AppCoordinator.showCaptureTooltip then anchors the label to the overlay's own top-left corner: measured at (20, 1049) on screen while the button sits about 1600pt away. The label IS being shown, in the corner of the screen, which reads to a person as no tooltip at all.

Adversarial review of the fix before building it. Keeping the bespoke route and repairing the preference would leave two tooltip systems in the app that look and behave differently (plain capsule under the pointer vs the design-language plate with a beak, different delays, different grace period). The shortest version that delivers more value is to delete the bespoke one: the shared HintAnchorView reads the control's real screen frame from AppKit, so there is no preference to go wrong, and it already carries the rest delay, the swap, the grace period and the escape from the window. One risk found and handled: the shared tooltip prefers to sit ABOVE its control, which on a strip pinned to the top of the screen would cover the capture thumbnail the buttons belong to, so the anchor needs to be able to ask for below.

Shipped. HistoryOverlay now uses the app's one tooltip (.toolTip on HintAnchorView) for Copy, Edit, Show in Finder, Delete, Play, the video Copy menu, the filter and Clear All. HintTooltip gained a preferred side (toolTip(..., below: true)) because this strip is pinned to the top of the screen and a label above a button would cover the capture it acts on; the screen still flips it when there is no room. Deleted TooltipController.swift, AppCoordinator.showCaptureTooltip/hideCaptureTooltip and HistoryOverlayController.panelFrame; hideHistory and the dismiss handler now call HintTooltipController.shared.dismiss().

Guarded by Scripts/playtest/history-tooltips-walk.json, which rests on all six controls in the Capture History panel and photographs each one. A hover step names the control by the words its tooltip shows, so if a label is dropped the step fails with 'no control with a tooltip starting "Delete"' rather than passing quietly. Two harness changes made it possible: hover takes an optional window (the history is a floating panel, not the editor window), and a -sc.png now covers the window PLUS anything hung on it, since a tooltip is a window of its own and a picture of the parent alone was squeezing the family into the parent's frame at 92%.

Second review, on the built thing. The labels read well and follow the pointer between glyphs. Two things left rough and written into the audit: the filter's label repeats what its own segments say, which I would cut but the task asked for the top row to keep its labels; and a label hangs past the bottom edge of the glass, which is the price of not covering the capture. Scripts/test.sh green (3367 tests). Scripts/playtest/tool-tips.json still green, so the tool bar is unaffected.
